industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the tape's disagreement now the loudest in the table and the row named as the likeliest source of the tilt scorecard's negative spread. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: C now, D prior at the industry, with Hotels A, Online retail A, Physical retail B and Apparel B: the market is buying the European consumer. The reasons that set F (United States consumer surveys falling, the European consumer never read, a regime that sells discretionary spend) could not be re-tested: no consumer survey for any G10 country was in window this week. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Held because nothing on the causes side changed and a move on the tape alone against two unread legs would be a moved goalpost; the exceptions stay at sector level (Physical retail C). Counter-case: a double notch on 138 stocks against four sectors at A or B on relative strength shuts bottom-up work out of the Lists for the industry where cheap good businesses accumulate, and eight weeks of negative tilt spreads are consistent with this row being wrong. To D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or a second industry reading at C or better with Hotels and Online retail holding A.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): high-multiple platforms hit by the discount rate and property-linked classifieds hit by rates twice; the turning note contradicts itself on this sector (Rightmove turning in its first hypothesis, Hemnet and Vend collapsing on its falling side with Hemnet 71% below its one-year high), which is a reason to hold the row rather than move it. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-09 against 2026-08-07, not week on week: F now, F prior. Counter-case: asset-light cash generators priced for zero terminal growth are where re-ratings start.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the re-test written last week (Neutral against Underweight after the Bank of England's decision and guidance on 5-Nov-26) could not run, because no source in the pack reports the outcome; the only United Kingdom items are undated headlines (the pound firmer on policy divergence; shoppers 'more upbeat than their European counterparts', City AM, against a GfK 'weakens in November' headline most likely from 2025). Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). The Budget read of last week stands: a UK-specific fiscal tail risk removed without lowering the rate; 22 of the Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Counter-case unchanged: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance when the 5-Nov-26 decision is read, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

memo.verdict: Bullish; progress to Early-Stage; conviction medium-low (a working hypothesis with a dated test); in a starting size that respects the binary. The park rule does not park: management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) C, business quality (E 2, BB 2) B, predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) B, trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) C, no D or F. Reasons to progress rather than park: the price already carries the fears; the downside on the multiple alone is bounded at 13 to 23%; the buyback retires about 1% of the shares a month while we wait; the next six months hold two dated tests, the Competition Appeal Tribunal certification hearing in November 2026 and the FY2026 results on 26 February 2027 with the margin above its 67% floor. Reasons for the size and the qualifier: the three-year return clears the 20% bar by less than one point (20.7% a year); the re-rating leg is sector-driven and not ours to earn; the environment of the week of 9 October 2026 is against the pattern. Drop the view on: retention below 90%; core ARPA growth below 5%; a certified claim with a fee-cap remedy on the table.
case: Thesis. Rightmove is a cause-for-concern-clearing case on an oversold, high-quality business, not a growth case. At 490.5p the shares pay 13.2x two-year-forward earnings for a portal with 90% of UK consumer property-portal time and 96% agency retention, because the market priced three fears at once (AI disintermediation; a 70% margin turned into 67% for good by a £60m programme; a New Homes cycle that keeps cutting the top line), and the fear that set the multiple is measurably absent so far. The return clears the 20% bar only if that fear is withdrawn from the multiple; without it the buyback and the price escalator deliver 15 to 16% a year on a downside bounded by a multiple already at the bottom of its own and its peers' ranges.

The change is mostly internal, already in motion and defensive. The board borrowed for the first time since listing (a £200m facility) to return over £400m by July 2027, about £330m buybacks retiring about 9% of the shares at today's price (the remaining £250m retires about 51m shares, 7% of the count; £74.0m done in H1 2026); the product engine was rebuilt (releases +40%, 84% agentic code, cloud complete 31 July 2026); tier migration lifts ARPA 7 to 8% a year without volume (Optimiser Edge 36%, Ascend 36% from 28% in six months, over 50% of agents above package). Guidance went down twice in nine months. Six of the twelve internal forces are at B or better (strategy change, standards, new products, real price rises, balance sheet, shareholder returns A); the screen's red flags are clean except the part-debt-funded buyback, accepted because the facility is 0.66x EBITDA and the multiple paid is a ten-year low. 'Internal forces' B; not A because no force lifts the top line.

The one external force that matters is a fear being disproved: under 0.5% of traffic from large language models, flat since December 2025; over 85% direct or organic; about 50% of listing metadata unscrapable; a Bernstein focus group (1 July 2026) found no shift in search behaviour; Scout24 and Swiss Marketplace show the same mechanism. The company's own tools cut the other way ("Ask Rightmove" users spend 40% more time on site; opex per release -16%). 'Disruption' (KQ 3, RA 1, E 1, BB 1) B; not A because the multiple at the 11th percentile says the market has not withdrawn the fear. The other external forces net to a mild headwind: demand D (transactions flat at 1.05 to 1.15 million against a 1.20 million average; new developments at a January 2017 low; new-build 17% of revenue; asking prices -2.0% in August 2026); political and regulatory D (the £1.56bn Newman claim, Innsworth-funded, certification hearing November 2026, legal costs £4m to £7m, a 2% profit drag; 1.5% of agencies, over 250, joined; over 2,000 signed a CMA petition; UK opt-out actions have low full-claim success rates); macro D (five-year fixed mortgage rates 4.7 to 5.1%; the hiking path re-marked up); competition C (OnTheMarket spent £46.5m in year one, three times Rightmove's budget, passed Zoopla on inventory, signed Connells, grew leads 14%, but holds 6 to 8% of traffic and has moved no output after two and a half years); the company's own cycle C (revenue growth 9.0% FY2025, 6.7% H1 2026; consensus trough +6.9% FY2026, +7.8% FY2027, +8.0% FY2028). 'External forces' C; 'Change Forces' C, not B because the screen wants three strong forces or a chief-executive change plus a guidance increase and guidance was cut twice.
counter_case: At the 'Investment Thesis': the pricing-power pillar fails. The portal's take is already 6 to 12% of a structurally low UK commission pool (over 6% per Jefferies, about 12% per Morgan Stanley), the highest among global peers; agents describe themselves as captive and call the platform a necessary evil; developers face 15 to 20% annual rises without added value at the bottom of a build cycle; CoStar has shown it will spend £46.5m a year to give agents a cheaper alternative and OnTheMarket now holds the second-largest inventory; and a £1.56bn opt-out claim, funded by Elliott's Innsworth and brought by a former CMA panel member, puts the pricing model in front of a regulator-like forum from November 2026, with a CMA petition of over 2,000 signatures showing the grievance is broad even if the mobilisation is thin. On this reading ARPA growth decays toward 1 to 2% (Jefferies), the 67% margin becomes a ceiling as defensive marketing is added (Morgan Stanley's 63% case; 65% by 2028), earnings-per-share growth falls to about 2%, the multiple stays at 13x or falls toward Autotrader's 10x, and fair value is 300p to 380p (Jefferies' severe case; Morgan Stanley's bear case); the certification in November is the catalyst that makes it visible. The risks report's own pre-mortem gives the NO profile the fewest hard inconsistencies in its Executive Summary.

At the 'Foundations': apparent retention is late-cycle and fragile, the cash metrics mask a systemic deterioration in agent relationships, and a certified claim would break the pricing model by collective withholding of fee increases (Jefferies); the 96% retention measures captivity, the 50%-plus above package are paying a tax they cannot avoid, and the tribunal is the first forum in which agents do not need each other's cooperation to act.
triggers: The Competition Appeal Tribunal certification hearing, November 2026: certification advancing the claim to trial is the Alarm level and the research's re-run trigger; a fee-cap remedy pleaded or a damages provision of size invalidates; a CMA market study opened would change the view on the claim condition. Large-language-model referral share above 2% of traffic, or a major model provider launching a property-search product with live UK listings and a measurable traffic effect, would change the view on the AI condition. Core ARPA growth below 5%, FY2026 ARPA growth below £100, or retention below 93% (Alarm) or 90% (Invalidate) would change the view on the pricing escalator. A second revenue guidance cut, or developments down more than 5% in a half, would change the view on New Homes; group revenue growth below 5% for a year invalidates. The FY2026 results on 26 February 2027 with the margin above the 67% floor; below 67% in a full year is the Alarm, below 65% invalidates. Buyback execution toward £330m by July 2027 and the next capital-return policy; paused is the Alarm, cancelled invalidates. OnTheMarket marketing above £50m a year (Alarm) or 15% of portal time (Invalidate). Earnings cuts of 2% or more at FY2027. The 24-month-forward multiple below 11.5x. The investment programme running over £60m or beyond FY2028. Strategic Growth Areas second-half growth below the 20 to 30% guided range. Unassessed: overlap with our own historical errors, because no track-record or lessons file was available; the candidate shapes are buying a de-rated quality name on the view that the fear will pass before the dated event that could confirm it, and paying for pricing power the customer resents. Unresolved in the research: the risks report's disagreement with itself on which pre-mortem profile wins; the unexplained Nationwide-to-NatWest mortgage-partner switch; whether the £60m programme ends on time in FY2028 with the margin recovering.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
